relationship_to_prior_review: This supplements, and does not change, the accepted six-declaration recognition packet reviewed under manifest a4068811e52cd1bacb5a2e1ab81d9a9de6e50149d93035a8be1a4ca16099bf5a. The explicit internal product assertion already has a written proof in Theorem 1 of that note. The new file formalizes that assertion and the behavior on each original factor.
independence: The reviewer read all eight declarations and their complete proofs, the full portable checker and scope, relevant exact mathlib definitions and proofs, and both earlier project component files. The reviewer supplied the C2 strict-containment counterexample during review; the author added it transparently before the final packet freeze. No core proof was authored by this reviewer.

hypotheses: P, B and all E_i are arbitrary groups; no finiteness of these groups is assumed.
K_i are normal subgroups of P.
rho_i is trivial on K_j for j different from i, and has trivial kernel on K_i.
The explicit finite product and equivalence require a finite indexing type J.
For the equivalence with ker(pi), the exact equality ker(pi)=sup_i K_i is required.
mathematical_scope.conclusion: Multiplication in P induces the displayed isomorphism from the product of the actual K_i to ker(pi). Its forward map is the given multiplication map, and a tuple supported in one factor maps to that factor's original subgroup inclusion.
mathematical_scope.weaker_hypotheses_for_intermediate_lemma: local_coordinates_independent uses neither normality nor finite indexing. It proves independence from the entire join of the other factors, not only pairwise trivial intersections. normal_local_factors_commute also has no finite-index assumption; finite indexing enters kernelProduct and the subsequent multiplication statements.
not_assumed: Commutativity or independence of the local subgroups as a premise
A global injectivity conclusion or the desired product isomorphism
Finite orders or equality of finite cardinalities

declaration_review.name: local_coordinates_independent
declaration_review.reason: The i-th coordinate kills each subgroup in the join of all other indices, hence kills that entire join. An element of K_i in this join is then trivial by local faithfulness. This proves iSupIndep, including for an infinite index type.

declaration_review.name: normal_local_factors_commute
declaration_review.reason: Normality places the commutator of x in K_i and y in K_j inside K_i. The i-th coordinate kills y and therefore kills that commutator. Local faithfulness makes it the identity; the standard commutator criterion gives Commute x y. The mathematical argument is independent of which of the two conventional commutator orientations is used.

declaration_review.name: kernelProduct
declaration_review.reason: This is Subgroup.noncommPiCoprod on the given subgroup inclusions, using the derived commutation theorem. Its underlying definition is Finset.univ.noncommProd of the actual subgroup elements. It is not an arbitrary chosen homomorphism.

declaration_review.name: kernelProduct_injective
declaration_review.reason: The mathlib injection theorem applies to the proved iSupIndep family and the subgroup inclusions. Its assumptions do not include the intended global conclusion.

declaration_review.name: kernelProduct_range
declaration_review.reason: The existing product-range theorem identifies the actual image with the join of the K_i. This is a theorem about the constructed map, not a separately posited product decomposition.

declaration_review.name: kernelProductEquiv
declaration_review.reason: MonoidHom.ofInjective restricts this same multiplication map to its own range. MulEquiv.subgroupCongr then identifies that range with ker(pi) by the proved range equality and hkernel. The subgroup transport is the identity on underlying group elements. The noncomputability concerns constructing an inverse, not changing the forward map.

declaration_review.name: kernelProductEquiv_apply
declaration_review.reason: The displayed forward-value equation is definitional (rfl), confirming that the equivalence really multiplies the given factors.

declaration_review.name: kernelProductEquiv_mulSingle
declaration_review.reason: After the forward-value equation, mathlib's pure-factor product theorem sends Pi.mulSingle i x to x in P. Thus the equivalence respects the original subgroup inclusion of each factor. Decidable equality is used only for this tuple construction.

Commutator.Basic supplies normal-subgroup commutator containment and the commutation criterion. ofInjective and subgroupCongr were read in their actual pinned definitions.
retained_infrastructure_and_attribution.ParityMixComponents: Its componentAssembly uses the same mathlib multiplication map. The earlier proof obtains subgroup independence from marked intersection property and disjoint supports, and obtains subgroup commutation from commutation of the markers. Those are different hypotheses from the present coordinate/normality argument.
retained_infrastructure_and_attribution.ParityComponentCoordinates: Its componentEquiv also constructs an actual equivalence through the assembly map's image and has a forward-value theorem. Its componentCoordinate_local verifies the corresponding pure-factor behavior. The new supplement correctly acknowledges this existing project pattern.

The eight new declarations give their own independence-and-commutation route through mathlib; they do not rely on an unstated application theorem from the companion module.
retained_infrastructure_and_attribution.priority: No historical novelty claim is justified or made. This is a formal completion of the already written generic direct-product conclusion, using established library infrastructure.

verification.strict_containment_control: In P=B=C2 with pi=id, one factor K=P and rho=id, normality and all coordinate hypotheses hold and ker(pi) is contained in K. But the kernel has order 1 and the factor product has order 2. Therefore equality, rather than mere containment, is essential for the asserted equivalence onto the base kernel. The final checker verifies the actual finite operation and maps for this counterexample.
verification.changed_source_control: The independent negative_control.py uses the portable --source-dir route and changes the product source bytes. The checker rejects the altered source at its exact binding before compiling that module, under Python -O.
